children: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has launched a benchmark-sized dual-tranche US dollar-denominated sukuk offering with initial price thoughts (IPTs) set at around 100 basis points over US Treasuries for the five-year tranche and around 110bp over for the 10-year tranche.

The sukuk, structured as senior unsecured trust certificates using an ijarah format, will be issued by KSA Ijarah Sukuk Limited, with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, acting through the Ministry of Finance, serving as seller and lessee.
The 144A/3(c)(7)/Reg S format offering comprises benchmark-sized five-year and 10-year tranches maturing on Sept. 9, 2031 and Sept. 9, 2036, respectively.
Pricing is scheduled for Sept. 1, 2026, with settlement expected on Sept. 9, 2026 (T+5).
The sukuk are expected to be rated Aa3 by Moody’s and A+ by Fitch, in line with the Kingdom’s sovereign ratings. Both agencies assign a stable outlook to the sovereign.
Proceeds from the issuance will be used for general domestic budgetary purposes.
The sukuk will be listed on the London Stock Exchange’s Main Market.
Citi, Goldman Sachs International, HSBC, J.P. Morgan and Standard Chartered Bank are acting as global coordinators and joint bookrunners.
Passive joint lead managers are Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, BNP Paribas, Dubai Islamic Bank, Fubon Bank, ING, Intesa Sanpaolo, Aljazira Capital and Société Générale.
Books opened on Tuesday and FCA/ICMA stabilisation will apply.
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Saudi Arabia launches dual-tranche dollar sukuk; IPTs at T+100bps and T+110bps
